English: Clay Basin
A simple clay-lined basin dug into the earth to collect and store water for the tribe. Provides a basic communal source of fresh water, supporting population growth and unity.
Stone Fountain
An expertly crafted stone fountain, fed by underground channels or manually filled, becomes the heart of the encampment. Its presence encourages growth and stability.
Sanctified Room
A sanctified chamber, often a rich tent or small timbered hut, dedicated to ritual purification. Used for sacred water rites and prayers, it fosters devotion and unity.
Water Pavilion
A spacious wooden pavilion surrounds the central fountain, sheltering ritual gatherings. The structure supports larger gatherings and provides clean water for the tribe.
Priests Chamber
A dedicated chamber for the tribes Mobad, the Zoroastrian priest. It is used for scriptural study, meditation, and leading water rites, strengthening religious authority.
Blessed Hall
A large tented or wooden hall where the faithful gather for communal rituals and water blessings. Its presence inspires piety and clan unity.
Holy Pavilion
A grand pavilion, richly decorated and consecrated, serves as the focal point for grand ceremonies and water festivals, attracting pilgrims and boosting prestige.
Sanctuary Room
A sanctum within the holy pavilion dedicated to the sacred purification of water and souls. Used for secluded meditation, rites, and fostering deeper unity.
Water Sanctuary
A revered sanctuary, with marble or stonework, pools, and channels for water purification rituals. It is a site of pilgrimage, greatly enhancing unity and priestly authority.
Zoroastrian Water Pavilion
The ultimate sanctum for Zoroastrian nomads: a magnificent, fortified pavilion with sacred pools, fire altars, and priestly quarters. It represents the tribes unity, piety, and spiritual guidance.
